why.title: Why the Medium Popcorn Exists #explained #popcorn #psychology
why.why: It explains a mundane, high-frequency consumer behavior (buying the middle option) through the lens of psychological biases, turning a daily habit into a fascinating insight about decision-making.

hook_patterns: Pairing a mundane daily annoyance with a specific, obscure psychological term to make the viewer feel 'seen' and educated simultaneously.
Visualizing abstract internal emotional states (trust, rejection, anxiety) through simple, contrasting actions between two characters.
Using a 'you vs. your brain' or 'you vs. society' dynamic to externalize internal conflict in a humorous, low-stakes skit.
todays_angle: Externalize the internal monologue of social anxiety or decision fatigue by having Leo and Mia physically act out their conflicting brain voices in a chaotic, fast-paced skit.
ideas: Leo tries to order coffee while Mia physically pulls him back and forth between 'healthy option' and 'sugar rush' options, representing the Zeigarnik effect of unfinished decisions.
Mia forgets a word in the middle of a sentence, and Leo becomes a literal 'buffering' icon, illustrating the cognitive load of language processing under stress.

Leo sees someone he knows across the street; Mia physically drags him away from the greeting (avoidance) while a ghostly version of Leo waves hello (social expectation), demonstrating the fight-or-flight response in social settings.
avoid: Generic '5 signs you're depressed' listicles, which are over-saturated and lack the narrative punch of a skit.
Over-explaining the scientific jargon in the first 3 seconds; the animation must do the heavy lifting before the explanation lands.
